Interface ClientActivityDetector

All Known Implementing Classes:
InMemoryClientActivityDetector
public interface ClientActivityDetector
Notices when more than one client (a tab, a window, a device) is working on the same thing at once, and who they are (issue #273).

Every request that touches the thing says which client sent it, by a random identifier the client made for itself, and the application says who that client is, as a ClientIdentity. The detector remembers which clients it saw on each resource key (any string, such as "draft:42") within the window, and answers who, other than the caller, was among them, and whether the caller arrived after all of them. It is advice, not a lock.

Authorization is the caller's job. The detector answers anyone who asks, and tells them names. The application must check that the caller may use the resource before it records the caller or asks who else is there, or the answer would let anyone probe resource keys to learn who is working where.

This package depends on nothing else in the application, so that it could be lifted out as a library of its own. The implementation here keeps its state in memory; see InMemoryClientActivityDetector for what that means for more than one server.

  • Method Details

    • record

      void record(String resourceKey, String clientId, ClientIdentity identity)
      Notes that this client, who is this person, has just been seen on the resource.

    • othersActive

      List<OtherClient> othersActive(String resourceKey, String clientId)
      The other people active on the resource within the window, one for each person, in order of label. A person is marked OtherClient.samePerson() if they are the same person as the caller, which means the caller has another tab or window open. The caller's own client is never among them. A caller who has not been recorded is nobody's same person.

    • leave

      void leave(String resourceKey, String clientId)
      Notes that this client has gone (issue #284): its tab or window was closed or left. It stops counting at once, instead of when the window has passed. Delivery of such a goodbye is not guaranteed, so the window stays as the fallback. A client that was not recorded is no change.

    • arrival

      Arrival arrival(String resourceKey, String clientId)
      When this client arrived, as against the others active on the resource: see Arrival. A caller who has not been recorded is told it did not arrive last, and at time zero.

    • window

      Duration window()
      How long a client counts as active after it was last seen: the heartbeat interval times the number of heartbeats that may be missed.

    • heartbeatInterval

      Duration heartbeatInterval()
      How often an open client should send a heartbeat.

    • suggestedHeartbeatSeconds

      default long suggestedHeartbeatSeconds()
      The heartbeat interval in whole seconds, rounded up and never less than one.

    • note

      default void note(String resourceKey, String clientId, ClientIdentity identity)
      Records the client if it named itself usably (see ConcurrencyHeaders.usable(String)); does nothing otherwise. For requests that are not heartbeats, such as saves.

    • heartbeat

      default Presence heartbeat(String resourceKey, String clientId, ClientIdentity identity)
      The answer to a heartbeat: records the client, then says who else is active, how often to beat, and whether it arrived last (issue #284). A client that did not name itself usably is not recorded and is told of no one.
